# HMAC Session Tokens Over JWT

**Decision.** [[project-management-web-platform]] issues session credentials as a base64url
JSON payload and an HMAC-SHA256 tag, using node:crypto rather than a JWT library.

~~~text
base64url(JSON({ u, r, iat, exp })) . base64url(HMAC-SHA256(payload, secret))
~~~

The session secret comes from validated configuration. The payload identifies the account and
records its issuance and expiry; request authentication reloads the account before building the
current actor.

## A small, fixed protocol

The token implementation has one signing algorithm: HMAC-SHA256. It has no caller-supplied
algorithm field, and verification compares the expected tag in constant time before parsing the
payload. It also rejects malformed structures, invalid claims, expired tokens, and timestamps
that are too far in the future.

Keeping those checks in one short module makes the token boundary visible. The accompanying
node:test suite covers valid issuance, forgery, tampering, expiry, malformed input, and bearer
header parsing.

## Why this format fits here

The API is a single service with one runtime dependency, Express. Node provides the HMAC
primitive through its standard library, so this format does not introduce a second runtime
package for a single verifier.

This is not a general recommendation to avoid JWTs. A maintained JWT library is a good fit when
other services must validate the same credential or when a standard interoperable representation
is required. In that situation, the project's own source recommends adopting the maintained
library rather than porting this format.

## The trade-off is interoperability

These credentials are intentionally local to this service. Another verifier would need an
agreed protocol and compatible key handling, so interoperability is the point at which the
format's small surface area stops being an advantage.

The format also does not make the service stateless. The API chooses to reload the named account
on each authenticated request so a block, deletion, or role change takes effect from current
data. That complementary decision is described in
[[re-read-the-account-on-every-request]].
